target_customer: Drug developers and patient advocacy groups who sponsor testing; patients with suspected rare genetic disease who receive free sponsored tests
problem: Rare disease patients wait years for a diagnosis, and drug developers struggle to find and reach undiagnosed patients.
business_model: Sponsored testing programs paid by pharma and foundations, plus data platform, with most patients not paying out of pocket
product_category: Genetic testing and patient intelligence platform for rare disease

founders.name: Lukas Lange
education: University of Oxford, PhD (bioinformatics and genetics), Rhodes Scholar
founders.background_notes: Employers and Rhodes Scholar from the YC page; TechCrunch June 2019 calls him a PhD candidate at Oxford.

founders.name: Harley Katz
education: University of Cambridge, PhD in theoretical astrophysics
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO by TechCrunch on 2019-06-18; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: 23andMe
competitors.what: Direct to consumer genetic testing, contrasted by TechCrunch with Probably Genetic's physician ordered tests

technical_complexity.rationale: Relied on an outside CLIA and CAP accredited lab and a bioinformatics partner; hard parts were physician network, compliance and later machine learning to find patients online.

defensibility.rationale: Patient registry and advocacy group relationships compound over time (130,000 patients claimed on its site), while testing itself is commoditized by labs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it by the sources found; company remains independent and active.

market_need_then: In 2019 TechCrunch describes genetic testing priced under 1000 dollars for children with autism; the later rare disease focus rests on long diagnostic odysseys cited by Fierce Healthcare.

identity.logo: A later rebrand uses lower case, thin curved letters, with the p and g open to interpretation, per the company blog as summarized by search

rebrands.why: Company blog post titled New Brand Explained; date and reasons not read directly because the page returned 404 on fetch

branding.community_and_virality: Works with more than 50 patient advocacy groups per its site, which is partnership more than virality.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable quirky name but little press about the brand itself; growth driven by pharma sponsored programs.

pivots.from: Physician ordered exome testing for children with autism (2019)
pivots.to: Rare disease patient intelligence platform with sponsored testing
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page now describes the rare disease platform. Date not found.

outcome_analysis: Probably Genetic launched in 2019 with autism exome testing backed by Khosla and TenOneTen, then shifted to rare disease, where pharma and foundations pay for free patient testing and data. Fierce Healthcare reports a 12M Series A. It is active with 17 people per YC, and sources do not show a shutdown or exit.
notes: The Fierce Healthcare article returned 403 so it was not opened; the 12M Series A figure comes from the search result headline and snippet. CB Insights lists 10.72M in November 2023 and Seedtable lists 10M, both aggregators and unverified, so the date is recorded as 2023 only. Investors for the Series A not verified (CB Insights names Threshold Ventures). YC says founded 2019 while the company site says 2018. A YC page link shows a Fierce article date in 2026 which conflicts with other sources and is ignored. Pivot date not found.
